---
title: Cache
description: Choose where to cache in VitNode - TanStack Query in the app, Redis inside your Hono API routes, or the HTML of public server-rendered pages.
icon: Zap
---

VitNode caches in three places. The app keeps API responses in TanStack Query, so a page never asks for something it already has. The API keeps expensive results in Redis through `c.get("cache")`, so a slow query runs once for everyone. The page cache stores the rendered HTML of public pages, so an article renders once for all its visitors. All three are opt-in: nothing is cached until your code asks for it.

## Pick a layer

| You want to                                                     | Use                        | Guide                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Render SSR data without refetching it, and skip repeat requests | App cache (TanStack Query) | [Cache app data](/docs/dev/cache/app)        |
| Stop running the same slow database query for every visitor     | API cache (Redis)          | [Cache API data](/docs/dev/cache/api)        |
| Look up `remember`, `delete`, `flush` and the other methods     | API cache (Redis)          | [Cache reference](/docs/dev/cache/reference) |
| Render a public page once and send that HTML to every visitor   | Page cache                 | [Cache server-rendered pages](/docs/dev/cache/pages) |

Most features use both. The API caches the expensive part once, and each visitor's app keeps its own copy of the response.

<Callout type="info" title="The fetcher never caches">
  [`fetcher()`](/docs/dev/fetcher) forwards the visitor's cookies, so a stored
  response could be one visitor's data served to another. That is why caching
  lives in the two layers above and not in the fetcher.
</Callout>

Content Engine public reads are not cached on the server. To cache them in your app or a separate front end, see [Content Engine caching](/docs/content-engine/caching).
